meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'My general attitude to life is to enjoy every minute of every day'?
meta.ogDescription: Credibly Branson’s. The cited 2008 Guardian interview could not be reached, and a second sentence usually goes missing.

answer.label: Attributed to
answer.authorDates: b. 1950 · English entrepreneur, founder of the Virgin Group
answer.sourceLine: Credibly his, and precisely dated by the one source that bothers to date it — but not confirmed. Wikiquote gives “his interview in The Guardian newspaper, 20th September 2008,” with no headline, author or link, and we could not reach that article to check the wording. The quotation also usually stops early: it goes on, “I never do anything with a feeling of, ‘Oh God, I’ve got to do this today.’”

source.heading: The source

docMeta.dd: Wikiquote’s Richard Branson page — no headline, author or URL given
Attributed — the cited article was not located

source.excerpt: “My general attitude to life is to enjoy every minute of every day. I never do anything with a feeling of, ‘Oh God, I’ve got to do this today.’”
trail: Wikiquote carries both sentences on its Richard Branson page ↗ and sources them to “his interview in The Guardian newspaper, 20th September 2008” — a date, but no headline, byline or link.

The article could not be found. theguardian.com is unreachable from the environment this page was built in. The Internet Archive’s Wayback Machine can serve a known URL, but its index cannot be searched by pattern without authorisation, so there was no way to identify which 20 September 2008 piece is meant.
So the date is Wikiquote’s, not ours. We reproduce it as the citation on offer and have not independently confirmed that the interview exists or that it carries this wording.
source.excerptNote: The second sentence is the one that gives the first any content — it is not a resolution to be cheerful, it is a claim about never doing anything reluctantly. This is Wikiquote’s text; we have not seen the newspaper page.
source.rightsNote: A 2008 newspaper interview with a living subject — comprehensively in copyright, and nowhere near the public domain. We have not identified the article, so we name Branson as the speaker rather than asserting a publisher.

author.name: Richard Branson
author.heading: Who said it
author.metaLine: born 1950 · English entrepreneur · founder of the Virgin Group
author.bio: Sir Richard Charles Nicholas Branson was born in Blackheath, London, in 1950, is dyslexic, and left Stowe School at sixteen to start a magazine called Student. A mail-order record business followed in 1970 and the first Virgin Records shop in 1972; the brand later carried an airline, a rail franchise and a spaceflight company. He was knighted in 2000 for services to entrepreneurship.

misattribution.heading: What gets lost in the quoting
misattribution.intro: Not a misattribution — nobody else claims it. But two things fall off on the way to the poster.

items.who: the version that stops at “every minute of every day”
items.why: Wikiquote ↗ continues: “I never do anything with a feeling of, ‘Oh God, I’ve got to do this today.’” Without it the line is a platitude; with it, it is a fairly demanding claim about how he spends his time.

items.who: the date that travels without the article
items.why: Wikiquote pins it to a Guardian interview of 20 September 2008 and gives no headline, author or link, and reprints repeat the date without ever naming the piece. We could not reach the newspaper’s archive to identify it, so the date remains a citation we are passing on rather than one we checked.

misattribution.truthLine: Wikiquote’s full text: “My general attitude to life is to enjoy every minute of every day. I never do anything with a feeling of, ‘Oh God, I’ve got to do this today.’” — Richard Branson on Wikiquote ↗
